title: Signal-priority 1:1 play — prep and async follow-up
content:
Purpose: reduce noise, re-anchor priorities, unblock next sprint deliverables. This doc is manager-prep + an async template to send after the 1:1. Keep to 25 minutes.

Meeting length: 25 minutes (recommended cadence: weekly / 1:1).

Timeboxed agenda (25m)
- 0-3m: Quick check-in (mood, capacity). One-sentence mood + focus level.
- 3-10m: Status snapshot (what moved, biggest blocker). Use the one-line rubric: Green = on-track, Amber = risk but mitigations exist, Red = needs help now.
- 10-18m: Deep dive topic (current priority). Rotate weekly: tech unblock / career / process. This week: tech unblock for gpt-scaling latency regression.
- 18-23m: Action items and owner commitments (explicit owners + dates).
- 23-25m: Parking lot + asynchronous follow-up plan.

Manager prep notes (to self):
- Pull last 7 days of relevant signals before the meeting: PR reviews (PR #1842), CI flakiness, p99 latency, batch queue length, oncall handoffs.
- Check the experiment status on quantization branch (bench table in PR). Note expected throughput gain vs regression at seq_len=1024.
- Confirm if INF-2145 (KV-cache eviction policy) is blocking the rollout — talk to Lina if unclear.
- Be ready to propose a small mitigation: temporary routing of high-latency tenants to dedicated cluster while infra team triages.
- Bring up the "signal reduction" experiment hypothesis: stricter alert thresholds for prefix-cache misses reduced page noise in canary last week. Ask for concrete numbers they observed.

Suggested deep-dive prompts (pick 1):
- "Walk me through the last deploy that caused the p95 spike — where did we expect the delta?"
- "If we had to freeze scope for one week to stabilize, what exactly would you roll back or toggle?"
- "What's the smallest experiment that would give us confidence the quantization change is safe at seq_len 1024?"

One-line status rubric (ask them to categorize):
- Green: Shipping and metrics look stable (no action needed).
- Amber: Shipping but with elevated risk (owner + mitigation within 48h).
- Red: Blocked or regressing (manager/engineering lead support required today).

Note-to-self: avoid turning 1:1 into a deep debugging session. If the problem needs >15m, schedule a follow-up sync with the small cohort and grab relevant logs/bench runs.

Action items template (fill during meeting):
- Owner: (name) | Item: (short) | Why: (one line) | Due: (YYYY-MM-DD) | Blockers: (if any)
Examples to seed in meeting:
- Owner: Lina Choi | Item: Add per-tenant throttling toggle to canary route | Why: reduces impact of noisy tenants on p99 | Due: 2028-05-17 | Blockers: infra capacity for toggle
- Owner: Arjun Rao | Item: Draft rollback play and rollback-on-failure thresholds | Why: shorten decision latency during rollout | Due: 2028-05-15 | Blockers: need SLT approval for automatic fallback
- Owner: Sofia Martinez | Item: Run focused perf-suite for quantization@1024 | Why: confirm no tail regressions | Due: 2028-05-18 | Blockers: limited GPUs in test pool

Async follow-up template (send within 4 hours after 1:1):
- TL;DR: (one line status: Green/Amber/Red)
- Decisions made: (bulleted)
- Action items: (copy filled template above)
- Materials attached: links to PRs, logs, bench results (if available)
- Next sync: (date/time or "async")

Parking lot (defer unless time allows):
- Career: book 30m next week for career conversation if the report indicated interest in promotion prep.
- Process: discuss if weekly signal filtering thresholds should be a team-level config (longer discussion), create RFC if they want to pursue.

Unresolved questions to bring up with Eng Lead/Infra if Red or sustained Amber:
- Can we get temporary burst capacity on dedicated pool for noisy tenant triage? (Infra SLA/commit?)
- Are there feature flags that allow gradated rollouts per region to reduce blast radius?
- Who owns the postmortem if rollback is triggered during a business hour? (defines follow-up ops)

Quick checklist before ending the sync:
- Confirm owner + due for each action item.
- Confirm how we'll validate progress (metric and quick test). Example: p99 latency back to baseline for 6 hours, or quantization bench shows <=1% throughput regression.
- Confirm async follow-up window (I send summary within 4 hours).

Notes to self (loose / scratch):
- If they are overloaded: help them prioritize and suggest dropping lower-impact stories (list 2 examples).
- Use "two-minute coaching": ask them to paraphrase the ask back to verify alignment.
- Keep the tone: curious + clarifying, not prescriptive.

End of doc.

Recent snapshot metrics to grab before meeting (where to get them):
- p99 inference latency (observability console: /dashboards/latency/1)
- batch queue length (infra-metrics /prometheus -> q_length_gpt_serving)
- PR review age (GitHub insights: open PRs >72h)
- Failure rate for canary route (SLO page)

If meeting goes long: schedule a 30m technical follow-up with logs and bench runner on the invite and bring in Lina + Sofia.

"If you can't express it in one sentence, you probably don't have a clear action." — keep that as closing guidance for both of us.
